reference: Peninsula: existing late-eighteenth-century coast reconstruction (guignes-1792). Cross-date geometry is an approximate display reference, not the observed shoreline in 1749. Modern reclamation is excluded.
interpretation: Gentle rubber-sheet alignment preserves eight landmark centres while allowing local scale, shear and curvature changes. Original shoreline traces are retained, with approximately 180 m-spaced controls along fourteen stretches. Each control moves halfway from the fixed-landmark spline toward its arc-length-paired reference position. Coast gaps, especially in the northwest, are deliberately retained to protect engraved lettering, streets and relief from excessive stretching. Cross-date reference curves express a display interpretation, not additional observations or a recovered eighteenth-century survey. The unmodified full source sheet is retained.

stretches.name: Mong Ha headland to east coast
stretches.method: Broad shoreline controls spaced approximately 180 m, moved 50% from the fixed-landmark spline toward the existing historical reference. Exact small-bay conformity is relaxed to retain engraved relief and labels.
